answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated, randomly assigned work that peers verify, with rewards released after a challenge window. A new identity starts with no track record, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply its verified contribution. To build influence, an attacker must fund each account and keep producing work that independent reviewers accept; failed or linked accounts lose their bond. A prism-style audit can expose copied outputs, while a vine of referrals earns no trust by itself, and nectar-like rewards arrive only after verification.
